To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we demonstrated the capability of PEEM as a new tool for mapping the near field and dynamic properties of LSPR on metallic nanostructures; (b) we showed that the near field of LSPR can be directly mapped with sub-10  nm resolution using PEEM; and (c) we demonstrated that the dynamics of LSPRs on metallic nanostructures can be probed with femtosecond resolution by combining PEEM and interferometric time-resolving techniques.

(1) We have developed a novel technique to map the field distribution of surface plasmons on metallic nanostructures using multiphoton photo-emission electron microscopy; (2) We have demonstrated the technique by mapping the field distributions of plasmons excited on gold nanostructures with various shapes; (3) We have shown that the technique can also be used to probe the dynamics (femtosecond timescales) of plasmonic fields.

(1) the field distribution and dynamics of localized surface plasmon on metallic nanostructures can be mapped by using multiphoton photoelectron emission microscopy (MP- PEEM) and (2) the field distribution is determined by both the geometry and the size of the nanostructure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the near-field properties and dynamic behaviors of LSPR on various metallic nanostructures.
the development of new methods and tools for the study of the optical properties of plasmon nanostructures and nanosystems.
the study of the dynamics and near-field mapping of surface plasmons on various engineered gold nanostructures.

this study provides an experimental demonstration that PEEM is a powerful tool for investigating the field distribution and dynamics of surface-plasmon resonances on metallic nanoparticles.
MP-PEEM is a powerful tool for studying the field distribution and dynamics of surface-plasmon resonances on metallic nanostructures.
this is an interesting and potentially powerful new method for studying plasmon resonant fields.

we have successfully demonstrated the direct imaging of the LSPRs in the near field using the PEEM technique.
we have developed a new method to investigate the near field and dynamic properties of surface plasmons in metallic nanostructures.
the combination of the MP-PEEM and the pump-probe technique provides a powerful tool to explore the spatially and temporally resolved near field of plasmonic structures.

MP-PEEM can be used to map the near-field distribution of plasmon resonant fields on a sub-10  nm scale and to investigate the dynamics of plasmon fields on femtosecond time scales.
the near-field distribution of surface plasmons in metallic nanostructures can be mapped by MP-PEEM with sub-10-nm spatial resolution and femtosecond temporal resolution.
MP-PEEM can provide a powerful tool to investigate the dynamics of plasmon resonant nanostructures.
